title: Descartes: I think, therefore I am
examples: What is the difference between thinking and existing?
What does 'I think, therefore I am' really mean?

explain.say: Descartes suggested we should doubt everything we think we know.

draw.text: Descartes: I think, therefore I am

explain.say: He questioned our senses, saying they sometimes trick us.
He imagined a dream life, where nothing was real.
But he realized one thing he could not doubt at all.
This led to his famous conclusion: I think, therefore I am.
In daily life, this means questioning assumptions about what is true.

faq.q: What does 'I think, therefore I am' actually mean?
faq.a: It means that even if everything else is false, the act of doubting proves you exist as a thinking thing.
asks: What is the meaning of the Cogito?

faq.q: Did Descartes doubt everything, including mathematics?
faq.a: Yes, he doubted everything, even simple mathematical truths, to find an unshakable foundation for knowledge.

faq.q: Is this argument only about the mind, or does it apply to the body too?
faq.a: Initially, it focuses only on the mind, or the thinking substance, which he calls the 'res cogitans'.
asks: Does this prove my body exists?
Is the body included in this proof?

faq.q: What is the difference between doubting and being wrong?
faq.a: Doubting is an active process of questioning, while being wrong is accepting a false belief.
asks: Is doubting the same as knowing?
Can I doubt something I know for sure?

faq.q: Who was Descartes and why did he write this?
faq.a: René Descartes was a philosopher who sought absolute certainty in knowledge, which led him to this famous deduction.
asks: Why is Descartes important in philosophy?
What was his goal with this idea?

facts: Descartes used systematic doubt to question all beliefs.
The 'Cogito' is the famous phrase summarizing his conclusion.
He argued that the existence of the thinking self is undeniable.
The argument establishes the mind's existence first.

quiz.say: If you doubt your senses, what can you still be certain of?

options.show: The fact that you are doubting
options.say: The fact that you are doubting

options.show: The reality of the objects around you
options.say: The reality of the objects around you

quiz.why: Because doubting requires a doubter, proving your existence as a thinker.

wrong.0: Because you could be dreaming that other people exist.
wrong.1: Because the dream argument suggests physical laws might not apply.
wrong.3: Because your senses can be tricked by illusions or dreams.

quiz.say: When doubting everything, what is the philosopher seeking?

options.show: A truth that cannot be doubted
options.say: A truth that cannot be doubted

quiz.why: He needed a starting point for knowledge that was absolutely certain.

wrong.1: Because he only reached this after establishing his own mind first.
wrong.2: Because he found the senses unreliable.
wrong.3: Because his method was focused on internal certainty, not external geography.

quiz.say: If you are thinking, what does Descartes argue you must be?
quiz.why: The very act of thinking proves that something is doing the thinking.

wrong.0: Because the argument separates the mind from the body.
wrong.1: Because thinking is broader than just following rules.
wrong.2: Because he doubts all knowledge until he finds this one thing.
